note: Every value here was measured against a live engine. See spec/02-engine-matrix.md for the probe that produced each one, and verification/live/ for the probes themselves. Do not edit from memory — re-run the probe.

typeAxis.note: The canonical axis records WHAT THE ENGINE STORES, not what a consumer wants for its UI. Measured 2026-10-22; see spec/06-canonical-types.md.

affinity.note: SQLite's documented rule ORDER, measured on 3.51.3. The axis records AFFINITY, not the declared name: VARCHAR(40) -> text, INT -> integer, REAL -> real, BLOB or an empty declaration -> binary, and everything else (BOOLEAN, DATETIME, NUMERIC) -> numeric. Measured storage is not the affinity: a '1' in a BOOLEAN column reports typeof integer and a date string in a DATETIME column stays text — both are NUMERIC affinity, and neither is enforcement. Order matters: INT before CHAR, CHAR before BLOB, BLOB before REAL.

introspection.note: Measured 2026-10-21 on SQLite 3.51.3; see spec/02 section Introspection.

tables.sql: SELECT name AS table_name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY name

traps: PRAGMA takes no bound argument: PRAGMA table_info(?) is a syntax error. The table name MUST be inlined and quoted with identifierQuote.
table_info reports notnull=0 for an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY column, which cannot be null. Normalize nullable = rawNullable AND NOT isPrimaryKey.
The declared type is one string with the length embedded (VARCHAR(40)); there is no separate maxLength fact, so maxLength is null here.
defaultText is SQL text ('x', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP), not a value.

columnProbe.sql: SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('{table}') WHERE name = ?

traps: now() does not exist (no such function), and DEFAULT now() is a syntax error.
CURRENT_TIMESTAMP evaluates to TEXT, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' — no subsecond, no timezone. A name substitution from Postgres now() silently changes the value's type and precision, not just its spelling.

types.note: SQLite assigns AFFINITY and accepts any type name verbatim, so nothing here is enforced — the map is a RECOMMENDATION, not a constraint, and an unknown type name is NOT an error (measured). The load-bearing fact is jsonb -> TEXT: the extraction operators -> and ->> DO work (SQLite 3.38+), but containment/existence (@>, ?, ?|, ?&) and GIN indexes do not.

sqlite.identifierNote: The double quote is the portable one. Backtick and [bracket] also parse on SQLite-family engines as legacy forms — a renderer must not use them, or it stops being portable.

fts.ddl: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS {name} USING fts5({cols}, content='{table}', content_rowid='rowid', tokenize='{config}')
triggers: CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {name}_ai AFTER INSERT ON {table} BEGIN INSERT INTO {name}(rowid, {cols}) VALUES ({newCols}); END
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {name}_ad AFTER DELETE ON {table} BEGIN INSERT INTO {name}({name}, rowid, {cols}) VALUES ('delete', {oldCols}); END

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {name}_au AFTER UPDATE ON {table} WHEN {changedGuard} BEGIN INSERT INTO {name}({name}, rowid, {cols}) VALUES ('delete', {oldCols}); INSERT INTO {name}(rowid, {cols}) VALUES ({newCols}); END
traps: Do NOT maintain this index by hand. A direct DELETE on an external-content fts5 table raises 'database disk image is malformed' for a rowid that is not yet indexed — the normal first-store case — measured on SQLite 3.45.1 and 3.51.3. Removal requires the documented 'delete' command carrying the OLD column values, which is what the triggers supply.
Guard the UPDATE trigger on the INDEXED columns only. An unguarded trigger rewrites the index row on every flags/internaldate change, and a sync updates those on every pass.

match.searchFrom: {name} f JOIN {table} m ON m.rowid = f.rowid

columnProbe.sql: SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('{table}') WHERE name = ?

traps: now() does not exist, and DEFAULT now() is a syntax error.
CURRENT_TIMESTAMP evaluates to TEXT, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' — no subsecond, no timezone. A name substitution from Postgres now() silently changes the value's type and precision, not just its spelling.

types.note: AFFINITY, as on sqlite: any type name is accepted, nothing is enforced. Injection and extraction DO work: json_extract, json_valid, and the -> / ->> operators (measured). Containment/existence (@>, ?, ?|, ?&) and GIN indexes do not.

turso.identifierNote: The double quote is the portable one; backtick and [bracket] also parse here as legacy forms and must not be used.

fts.ddl: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS {name} ON {table} USING fts ({cols})
traps: fts_match's first argument is the COLUMN list, not the index name. Passing the index name parses and returns SILENTLY EMPTY.
The index is engine-maintained, so the external-content sync statements an fts5 table needs are deleted rather than translated.

introspection.note: Measured 2026-10-21 on PostgreSQL 16.15; see spec/02 section Introspection.

tables.sql: SELECT table_schema, table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_type = 'BASE TABLE' AND table_schema = ? ORDER BY table_name

columns.sql: SELECT table_name, ordinal_position, column_name, data_type, udt_name, character_maximum_length, is_nullable, column_default FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = ? ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position

primaryKeys.sql: SELECT tc.table_name, kcu.column_name, kcu.ordinal_position FROM information_schema.table_constraints tc JOIN information_schema.key_column_usage kcu ON kcu.constraint_name = tc.constraint_name AND kcu.table_schema = tc.table_schema WHERE tc.constraint_type = 'PRIMARY KEY' AND tc.table_schema = ? ORDER BY tc.table_name, kcu.ordinal_position

foreignKeys.sql: SELECT tc.table_name, tc.constraint_name, kcu.column_name, kcu.ordinal_position, ref.table_name AS foreign_table, ref.column_name AS foreign_column, rc.delete_rule, rc.update_rule FROM information_schema.table_constraints tc JOIN information_schema.key_column_usage kcu ON kcu.constraint_name = tc.constraint_name AND kcu.table_schema = tc.table_schema JOIN information_schema.referential_constraints rc ON rc.constraint_name = tc.constraint_name AND rc.constraint_schema = tc.table_schema JOIN information_schema.key_column_usage ref ON ref.constraint_name = rc.unique_constraint_name AND ref.constraint_schema = rc.unique_constraint_schema AND ref.ordinal_position = kcu.position_in_unique_constraint WHERE tc.constraint_type = 'FOREIGN KEY' AND tc.table_schema = ? ORDER BY tc.table_name, tc.constraint_name, kcu.ordinal_position

traps: Do NOT join constraint_column_usage by name: it matches every column of the referenced constraint against every key column, so a 2-column composite FK returns 4 rows including x->y and y->x. Measured.

Join the referenced side through referential_constraints.unique_constraint_name AND key_column_usage.position_in_unique_constraint. Joining it on the FK's own constraint name only looks right when both tables give their columns the same names.
data_type is normalised (character varying) while udt_name is the internal name (varchar); both are carried so a canonical type axis can decide later.
column_default is engine text and includes casts: 'x'::character varying, now(). Not portable.

identity.ddl: BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY
identity.note: BY DEFAULT, not ALWAYS: imports carry their own identifiers, so explicit ids must be insertable. ALWAYS rejects them (measured: cannot insert a non-DEFAULT value into column id) and would force an engine-specific OVERRIDING clause into every port.

schemaVersion.write: INSERT INTO _sure_store_meta (k, v) VALUES ('schema_version', ?) ON CONFLICT (k) DO UPDATE SET v = EXCLUDED.v

columnProbe.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = ? AND column_name = ?

traps: BEGIN IMMEDIATE is a SQLite construct; Postgres rejects it (syntax error).

caller-issued is a HAZARD here, not a prohibition. A transaction is bound to the CONNECTION, not the pool, so caller-issued requires binding ONE connection for the transaction's lifetime. A transaction-local query issued on a pool handle runs autocommit while the rest of the tx runs inside it — measured as a missing FOR UPDATE lock, not as leaked SQL. driver-managed avoids the hazard by construction. Both are declared because both work: measured, BEGIN; COMMIT; and SELECT … FOR UPDATE all succeed caller-issued on Postgres 16.15.
now() and CURRENT_TIMESTAMP are interchangeable here — unlike the embedded engines, where only CURRENT_TIMESTAMP exists and it returns TEXT.

canonical.note: Measured on PostgreSQL 16.15 across 21 types. citext is deliberately its own canonical type rather than text: collapsing it would silently drop the case-insensitivity a consumer chose the type for. Anything absent from this map is an ERROR, never 'other' — inet, interval, tsvector, money and xml are genuinely unmapped today.

types.note: Native types, and jsonb round-trips as jsonb. Every operator works — ->, ->>, @>, ?, ?|, ?& — and GIN indexes are available. The embedded engines have -> and ->> only.

postgres.identifierNote: Double quote only — backtick and [bracket] are syntax errors.

fts.ddl: ALTER TABLE {table} ADD COLUMN {name} tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('{config}', {expr})) STORED
fts.indexDdl: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS {name}_idx ON {table} USING GIN ({name})
traps: id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY PARSES and does NOT auto-assign. The DDL applies cleanly and inserts that omit id fail only at runtime.
PRAGMA user_version is a syntax error on read and write.
pragma_table_info does not exist; use information_schema.columns.
to_tsvector('english', ...) stems, so it matches more than unicode61 would. 'simple' is the parity config.

Hand-built to_tsquery('simple', 'a & b') THROWS on a term carrying tsquery metacharacters (syntax error in tsquery). Use plainto_tsquery, which takes the terms as plain text and produces the identical query for ordinary input — measured.

bindings.note: PARAMS and RESULT are BINDING facts, not engine facts — measured, and declaring them per ENGINE would be wrong. Evidence: SQLite's engine accepts `?`, `?NNN`, `:name`, `@name` and `$name`, but node:sqlite binds POSITIONALLY, so only `?` works through it (measured: `$1` and `:name` fail with 'column index out of range'). And the affected-row count is reported as `changes` by both SQLite-family bindings and as `rowCount` by pg, for the same underlying engine capability.

node:sqlite.paramsNote: Only `?` binds. The engine accepts more styles; this binding does not expose them positionally.

pg.paramsNote: `$n` only — `?` and `:name` are syntax errors (measured via PREPARE). Bound `LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2` is accepted.
pg.resultNote: No insertId field: an id comes back through RETURNING, not from the result envelope (measured on pg 8.23.0).
